_comment: Dfine brand tokens — SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Read by SKILL.md (instructions) and scripts/validate_brand.py (enforcement). Change a value here and both the guidance and the validator update together.

background.rule: Content slide backgrounds are ALWAYS pure white. The illustrations are composited on white, so any off-white (e.g. #F9FAFB) leaves a visible seam/halo behind them. The validator fails on any non-white slide background.
background.exception: See section_divider (OPEN THREAD): dividers will be allowed approved background images and a to-be-defined set of colours.

section_divider.note: Section dividers will use approved background IMAGES (going into the asset bank) AND a to-be-defined set of allowed background colours. Until that set is defined, the validator treats any non-white background as a violation. Revisit to (1) list approved divider bg images, (2) define allowed divider colours, (3) exempt dividers in the validator.

iris.role: SECONDARY accent (to teal) — alternating cards, chart series, highlights; also the bloom colour

scarlet.role: the signal — KEY EMPHASIS moments only (a hero metric, a CTA, a critical flag); sparing, a few per deck at most
scarlet.note: This is the Dream brand colour 'Champagne'; Dfine's deliberate colour link to Dream. NOT the rejected champagne-gold.

format.note: Widescreen only. Do not produce 4:3 or portrait decks.

accent_hierarchy: Teal is the primary accent (default). Iris is the secondary accent — use it alongside teal for alternating cards, chart series, and highlights. Scarlet is the signal — reserved for key emphasis moments, sparingly. Order when assigning accents: teal → iris → (scarlet only for the emphasis point).

layout_style.density: Sparse & premium by default — generous whitespace, few elements per slide, ideally one idea per slide. Flex denser only for data/sprint decks when the content needs it.
layout_style.spacing: Generous, consistent spacing as loose guidance (not a snapped scale). Comfortable side margins (~0.9in) and clear gaps between blocks.
layout_style.lists: Bullet lists are fine, styled minimally — a small dash or dot, generous line spacing. Prefer structured layouts (cards / rows) for key points, but don't force it.
layout_style.tables: Hairline grid (border/default) + a faint (surface/muted) header row. No zebra striping, no heavy fills. Minimal and clean.
layout_style.accessibility: Guidance, not enforced: keep body text ≥ ~12pt on slides; avoid low-contrast text — never use scarlet (#E8A58F) or light tints (iris tint #D9DEFC, mint) for small text on white. Text is navy / ink / muted; the light accents are for fills and large display only.

surface.rule: Subtle neutral fills — table header rows, faint card grounds. Page is always white.

border.rule: Field / card / input borders are neutral grey. Never teal or any accent colour for chrome.

status.rule: Status colours are role-based. Use -strong for fills/borders/dots, -text for coloured text on white (readable), -bg for tinted backgrounds. Never repurpose a status colour as a decorative accent.

heading.rule: Titles use Medium throughout (calm, refined, consistent). Bold exists in the family but titles default to Medium. Canonical name is exactly 'Bricolage Grotesque'. NEVER 'Bricolage Grotesque 14pt Medium' or any optical-size named-instance string — that fails to resolve on machines that have the font installed normally. Embed the clean OFL family.

body.note: macOS-native; licensed (not embeddable). Decks target a Mac audience. On Windows it substitutes — acceptable per audience.

paper_bg.reason: Was used as page background; replaced by pure white. Do not use for slide backgrounds.

policy.content_scope: The skill is the BRAND LAYER, not a content author. It does not decide content, copy, length, structure, or how the user drafts — that stays in the user's workflow. Its job is to render/enforce the Dfine brand on whatever presentation the user is building or editing.
policy.casing: Sentence case everywhere — kickers, labels, and titles. No ALL-CAPS or uppercase transform (matches the product-UI 'no uppercase labels' rule). Acronyms (IT, OT, CVE, AI) keep their natural caps.
policy.illustration_density: Sparing. Use illustrations on hero / section / statement moments; keep most content slides clean and typographic. Not every slide needs art.
policy.on_violation: Auto-fix drift silently (snap off-palette colour to the nearest token, wrong font to Bricolage/Avenir, non-white bg to white) and note what changed. EXCEPTION: if the user explicitly requested the off-brand value, do NOT override — warn them it's off-brand and suggest the on-brand equivalent, then let them decide.
policy.screenshots: Raster screenshots / photos are allowed anywhere and are EXEMPT from the colour check (their pixels aren't XML colours anyway). Chrome — text, shapes, borders, backgrounds — is always enforced.
policy.illustrations: Use only illustrations from assets/illustrations (the bank). Never generate or invent illustrations.
policy.icons: Use only icons from assets/icons (exported from the Figma DS set). Never invent icons or pull raw Lucide.
policy.logo: Use ONLY the Dfine logo files from assets/logos — never draw, recreate, or regenerate it (not as shapes, text, or a generated image); place the approved file unmodified. Placement: put it where it best fits the slide's content (not a fixed footer slot), then let the user move or remove it.
policy.missing_asset: If the bank has no matching illustration or icon, use a clean typographic layout instead. Never invent art or icons — absence is fine.
policy.charts: OPEN THREAD — chart / data-series colouring (bar, line, pie) is not defined yet. Do not improvise a chart palette; keep charts minimal and token-coloured, and flag that the palette still needs testing.
policy.verify_default: Always run scripts/validate_brand.py after building or editing a deck. Render a slide-image preview only when the user asks for one.
policy.off_brand_detection: If you notice off-brand elements in a deck the user is working on — part or all — FLAG them and ASK whether to bring them on-brand. Do NOT silently rewrite their deck; transform only on their go-ahead.
policy.photos: Photographs come ONLY from the photography bank (assets/photo — curated). Never pull arbitrary/stock images. Treatment and role are an OPEN THREAD (see photography).
policy.motion: Static by default — no slide transitions or build animations. Add motion only when the user explicitly asks, and keep it tasteful.
policy.confidentiality: No confidentiality/classification marker by default. If the user enables it, apply a small muted marker deck-wide.
policy.language: English by default; produce other languages on request. Bricolage/Avenir are Latin-script — non-Latin languages need a fallback font, so flag that if asked.
policy.icons_style: Bare icons in navy or muted grey by default. Put an icon in a small teal/iris chip/circle only when it needs more presence (e.g. feature highlights). Keep it flexible.
policy.pdf_export: Produce the .pptx by default. Export a shareable PDF only when the user asks.
policy.deck_starters: No fixed per-use-case skeletons. Provide the reusable layout library and assemble to the user's own structure — never impose a canned deck outline.
policy.no_emojis: Never use emojis in decks (or any Dfine material). Use an icon from the bank instead.
policy.logo_variant: Pick the logo variant that suits the background — the dark wordmark on white (default), a light variant on any dark moment (e.g. a dark section divider).
policy.speaker_notes: Leave speaker notes alone — they're the user's content. Write or edit them only on request.
policy.page_numbers: No page numbers by default (matches the no-fixed-footer, sparse-premium direction). Add them only on request.
policy.number_date: Light house style ONLY on text the skill itself generates: thousands separators (1,234), a consistent date format, tidy units/%. Never reformat the user's own content.

hero.problem: Hero covers usually place an image/video on one side (mostly right); the text on the other side must align to it and not collide. The model can't reliably see where an image's content actually sits.
hero.solution: Make the geometry DATA, not a guess. (1) Hero LAYOUTS bake the split — an image/video zone (right ~45%) plus a left text safe-zone placeholder; fill the placeholder. (2) Each hero asset in the manifest declares safe_zone and image_zone rectangles; a non-standard visual overrides the default split so text still lands clear. (3) The validator flags any text box overlapping image_zone on a hero slide.
hero.status: OPEN THREAD — build the hero layouts + per-asset safe_zone/image_zone metadata + the overlap check.

type_scale._status: RECOMMENDED guidance, NOT enforced by the validator. Titles in Bricolage Medium; body/caption in Avenir.
type_scale.caption: 10-11pt, muted

photography.status: OPEN THREAD — bank to be created
photography.note: A curated photography bank (assets/photo) so we control the kind of imagery shown. Then define treatment (full-bleed vs framed vs brand-tinted/duotone) and when photos are used vs illustrations. Bank-only, like illustrations/icons/logo.
